context.exploration_scope: Executed S22's connected, per-Principle trigger path a second time: compared each Principle's own real state against the S22 checkpoint (not S21's), and ran a judgment loop only for the Principle(s) whose real state actually changed, with synthetic change substitution structurally prohibited

problem: PHASE-SSI-S22 reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER on its own first check for both Principles -- the connection had not yet been exercised a second time to confirm the baseline genuinely advances to S22s checkpoint (not S21s) between checks, and there was an explicit temptation this phase had to resist: fabricating a state difference just to demonstrate the independent-verdict-vs-Principle-guided-verdict response path, rather than honestly reporting NO_REAL_TRIGGER again when the real data has not moved.

decision.decision_summary: P1 real_state_changed=false (left untouched). P2 real_state_changed=false (left untouched). synthetic_change_injected=false. 0 forced status changes. 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic policy, 0 automatic execution. Overall verdict: NO_REAL_TRIGGER.

action.action_summary: Compared each Principle's own last known real state (S22's trigger.current_state checkpoint) against a fresh read of the real trace/hold/overlay files; gated each Principle's judgment loop strictly on its OWN detected change with no fabricated substitute ever introduced; on change, computed the independent verdict before the Principle-guided verdict and compared them; never wrote to any real file.

evidence.evidence_detail: final_state=NO_REAL_TRIGGER, p1_real_state_changed=false, p2_real_state_changed=false, synthetic_change_injected=false, regression_all_passed=true, dangling=0, duplicates=0

result.note: Correctly reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER a second time against the advanced S22 checkpoint, with no synthetic change substituted -- confirms the trigger baseline moves forward each execution and stays honest under real data, rather than manufacturing a demonstration.

cause.root_cause_summary: A change-gated trigger that has only ever reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER faces a real design temptation to prove itself by faking a change on the next check -- but doing so would mean the response path was never actually validated against real data, only against a scenario invented to make the demonstration succeed; refusing that shortcut and re-reporting the honest negative is what keeps the trigger trustworthy.

lesson: Advancing a trigger's baseline a second time (S22 -> this phase, mirroring how S11 advanced S10's single-Principle baseline to two Principles) has to carry an explicit, structural prohibition on synthetic change: the code path that would compare a fabricated current_state simply does not exist here, so there is no way for a false PRINCIPLE_APPLICABLE/PRINCIPLE_REJECTED result to slip in dressed as a real one. Honestly repeating NO_REAL_TRIGGER is the correct outcome exactly as often as the real data warrants it, no more and no less.
